case noun

a container

also pencil case, glasses case, holder, sheath, wrapper

classical

Cic. Verr. 2.4.52: efferrī sine thēcīs vāsa
Traupman 287
M-O s.v. case (container)

thēca, thēcae f.

noun, first declension · Declension on Wiktionary

a case, a cover, a sheath

Greek θήκη: whatever a thing is kept in, from a sheath to the case of a silver cup.

Other words

  • thēca calamāria — a pen case; a pencil case

    also used · classical · Suet. Claud. 35 (Lewis & Short, s.v. calamārius); Traupman 287

    A case for reed pens (calamī); it serves for a pencil case.

  • capsa, capsae f. — a box or case, above all for books; a satchel

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Div. Caec. 51 (Lewis & Short); Hor. S. 1.4.22 (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    The box in which book rolls were kept and carried.

  • involūcrum, involūcrī n. — a wrapper, a cover

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Verr. 2.4.65: candēlābrī (Lewis & Short); Traupman 409 · Declension on Wiktionary

    Something wrapped round a thing, from involvō: a soft case or cover.

Examples

  • efferrī sine thēcīs vāsa

    silver vessels being carried out without their casesCic. Verr. 2.4.52

See also box, container, suitcase, pillowcase, school bag, pencil.
